title: Canary sample spectra & triage scratchpad
body:
Purpose:
This scratchpad captures a repeatable quick-path for investigating small canary vs prod latency deltas using a spectral approach: look at the distribution shape across sample buckets ("spectra") rather than just mean/95/99. Goal is to get to a hypothesis that can be validated with a focused microbenchmark or bisect within 60-90 minutes for a typical alert.

Context and rationale:
- We keep seeing subtle canary drift: mean latency stable but a shoulder forms in the 80-98th percentile band for certain customers.
- Standard dashboards (p50/p95/p99) are noisy and often hide multi-modal behavior.
- Spectra = histograms + token-path signature overlays to surface whether extra cost is coming from input preprocessing, attention KV growth, or model execution hot paths.

Quick triage checklist (first 10–20 minutes):
- Confirm the alert scope: which canary pool, which model variant, time window, and traffic split (canary %).
- Pull the canary vs prod spectral snapshot (Grafana panel id: serving-spectra, time range = alert window ±30m).
- Visual check: is there a new hump (secondary mode) or long tail stretch? Note the latency bucket ranges (e.g., 60-120ms vs 250-400ms).
- Cross-check recent deploys/rollouts: PRs in last 24h, config changes (batch size, quantization profile), autoscaler policy modifications.
- Check error budget/availability alarms — is the latency change accompanied by increased retries or 5xx?
- If erroring, stop canary, switch to fallback variant. If just latency, continue investigation.

Data to collect for deeper triage (put in a bisect ticket):
- Representative request IDs and traces (x-request-id) sampling from the high tail bucket (copy 20 unique IDs).
- Full trace flame graphs for those requests (span timings for preprocess, model-run, postprocess).
- Token counts and input length distribution for sampled requests.
- KV-cache hit/miss markers and cache growth over request lifetime.
- Per-shard GPU scheduling metrics and queue length for the same time window.

Spectral analysis steps (recommended panels and derived views):
- Latency histogram (log buckets) for canary vs prod overlay — use same smoothing kernel. Look for separated modes.
- Token-length vs latency heatmap — are longer sequences clustering to the new mode?
- Stage breakdown stacked bars (preprocess / enqueue / queue-wait / serve / postprocess) aggregated by bucket.
- KV-cache hit-rate overlay on tail buckets.
- CPU/GPU utilization sidecar and kernel time per request (if available).

Hypothesis generation model (quick templates):
- "Preprocess spike" -> evidence: preprocess stage accounts for >50% of extra time in tail samples, many different token lengths, no change in model-run kernel times.
- "Queue/packing regression" -> evidence: queue-wait grows, batch sizes fluctuate, spike coincident with increased arrival jitter.
- "KV growth or cache churn" -> evidence: model-run times increase disproportionately for long sequences with repeated context, cache miss flags present.
- "Kernel/compilation mismatch" -> evidence: new model variant or quantization uses different kernels; per-request kernel-time increased, reproduces in microbench.

Bisect plan (when a candidate commit/set of PRs identified):
- Narrow to suspect PRs for canary pool: apply binary search over commits using a small dedicated canary cluster with synthetic traffic reproducer.
- Reproduce with synthetic load that mirrors spectral shape (mix of short and long sequences based on production distribution).
- For each step in bisect, capture 5k requests, produce spectra and stage breakdown.
- Stopping criteria: clear delta in spectral hump or stage time consistent with earlier trace evidence.

Microbench recipes (quick scripts we keep in infra/tools):
- reproducer/generate-mix.py --ratio-short=0.7 --ratio-long=0.3 --seed=42 --seq-lens=16,512
- bench/run-serve-benchmark --variant=canary --model=redwood-v1-small --concurrency=32 --sampling=1
- helper: trace-collector --ids-file ids.txt --output traces/

Observability artifacts to attach in ticket:
- Spectra PNG (canary vs prod overlay)
- 10 trace flamegraphs (heavy tail samples)
- microbench results (latency distribution CSV)
- list of suspect PRs/rollouts with timestamps

Decision rubric (fast):
- If stage breakdown shows preprocess or routing >50% of delta: hotfix in routing/preprocess component and revert related config changes.
- If model-run kernel time is root cause and a PR changed kernels or quantization: revert or pin to previous kernel set and open rollback PR.
- If bisect not decisive within 3 commits, expand search window + add canary traffic mirrors to capture arrival pattern differences.

Notes & open questions (TODOs):
- Need a standardized "spectra export" artifact for every canary run (histogram + per-stage breakdown JSON) — Miguel to prototype exporter (JIRA-SRV-987).
- For attended tail investigations, add token-path fingerprinting to traces (small 64-bit signature) so we can group requests with similar attention growth without storing full inputs.
- Can we get per-kernel timing from the runtime for non-debug builds? If not, add lightweight counters in the kernel selection path.

Recent example (summary):
- 2026-02-26: Canary pool 'north-eu-1-canary' showed a new hump at 180-320ms.
- Evidence: token-length heatmap showed a cluster at seq len 256-384; trace flames pointed to model-run + kv-merge step.
- Action: ran microbench with high ratio of mid-length sequences, reproduced 2x increase in median model-run time. Bisect pointed to commit that changed attention cache eviction policy. Rolled back eviction tweak; hump disappeared.

If you're working an active alert, add notes here and ping @oncall-serv-runtime in Slack with the 'spectra' snapshot link. Use this scratchpad as the first record for the triage ticket so we have a consistent narrative for follow-ups.

Appendix: quick command snippets
- fetch traces: gcloud logs read --limit=100 --filter="resource.labels.cluster_name=serving-canary AND severity>=ERROR" --format=json > sampled.json
- run microbench: ./tools/bench/run-serve-benchmark --config canary-spectra.yaml --out results.json
- generate spectra PNG: python tools/observability/make_spectra.py results.json --out spectra.png

End of scratchpad.
